The test image shows soybean seedlings at germination stage in wet/muddy soil. Key features:
- One healthy green cotyledon (left)
- Middle seedling has brown, rotted hypocotyl tissue — collapsed at soil line
- Right shows a cross-section of rotted stem (brown interior)
- Wet, waterlogged soil conditions

This pattern strongly suggests a damping-off/seedling rot disease. Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia.

Let me view a Pythium damping off reference.

The reference image for Pythium_damping_off matches extremely well: same wet/dark soil, green cotyledon present, brown rotted hypocotyl/stem tissue at the soil line, seedling collapse at early germination stage.
